content:
If you're not in a rush to buy Apple products on launch day and are willing to wait, the Apple Certified Refurbished store has always been a solid option. Typically, about three months after a new product launches, refurbished versions start appearing on Apple's website for the first time.

Other companies offer similar options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but it's worth noting that the quality standards and warranty terms differ across these programs……

Apple Certified Refurbished

Shopping at the Apple Certified Refurbished store typically gets you around 15% off, and the products themselves are almost identical to brand-new ones. Specifically, Apple guarantees all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing performed by Apple
  • Brand new housing with no marks or scratches
  • Brand new battery with the same battery life as a new product
  • All original accessories and cables included
  • Same Apple one-year standard warranty as a new product
  • AppleCare+ can also be purchased

Essentially, the only difference you'll see is that the product comes in a plain white box rather than the original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed may have more competitive pricing, but keep in mind you won't get the same quality guarantees:

  • Inspection and testing is performed by the seller, not Apple
  • The housing is used and expected to have marks and scratches (see below)
  • The battery is used and only guaranteed to have at least 80% of original capacity
  • Accessories may not be Apple original products
  • Comes with an Amazon 90-day warranty instead of Apple's one-year warranty

Regarding marks and scratches, Amazon offers three quality grades:

  • Premium / Excellent: No visible cosmetic imperfections from 12 inches away
  • Good: Light scratches only, barely noticeable when holding the device from 12 inches away
  • Acceptable: Visible and tactile scratches

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored is much vaguer than Amazon, and what you're actually getting is described in very ambiguous terms:

  • No promises about cosmetic condition, only claims "like-new performance and reliability"
  • No specific information about battery condition beyond the above description
  • No information provided about accessories
  • Warranty is provided by the seller, not Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier comes with a one-year seller warranty, while Like New, Good, and Fair tiers only get 90 days. The company doesn't clearly define what each tier means.

9to5Mac's take

If you want something that's identical to a new product in terms of both appearance and Apple warranty, the Apple Refurbished store is clearly the top choice.

That said, Amazon Renewed pricing can indeed be significantly cheaper, and if you're willing to accept the trade-offs described above, it may be a decent option. Especially if you're planning to follow our advice and get an iPhone 17 Pro instead of this year's latest model to save money (you won't get cables either way), here are some pretty attractive deals:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,214 (originally $1,499) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,215 (originally $1,499) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,208 (originally $1,499) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,164 (originally $1,299) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,170 (originally $1,299) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,171 (originally $1,299) — Only $1 above all-time low price

As for Walmart Restored, I have reservations because their guarantees are too vague, but if you're not satisfied, you do have the option to return it.
